title: Emergency Dental Care
meta_title: Emergency Dentist in Alexandria, VA, Open 7 Days | WA Dental Care
meta_description: Toothache, broken tooth, knocked-out tooth, lost crown or abscess? West Alexandria Dental Care sees urgent problems during seven-day hours.
h1: Emergency dental care in West Alexandria
intro: A tooth that breaks on a Friday evening or starts throbbing on a Sunday morning still needs a plan. Our hours run from 7 AM to 8 PM on weekdays and 8 AM to 1 PM on Saturday and Sunday, so most urgent problems can be seen the same day. Call first, tell whoever answers what has happened, and we will fit you in.

sections.heading: Call us today if
items: A tooth hurts badly, keeps you awake, or throbs on its own.
A tooth is broken, cracked or has a sharp edge cutting your tongue or cheek.
A crown or filling has come off, especially if the tooth is sensitive.
There is swelling in the gum, a bad taste, or a bump that drains.
An adult tooth has been knocked out or pushed out of place. This one is minutes, not hours. Read [what to do for a knocked-out tooth](/emergency-dentistry/knocked-out-tooth/) now.
Bleeding after an extraction has not stopped after twenty minutes of firm pressure on gauze.

sections.heading: What happens at an emergency visit

items.title: You call, we plan
items.body: Describe what happened and whether there is swelling or fever. That tells us how urgently to see you and what to have ready.

items.title: Find the cause
items.body: A focused exam and a [digital X-ray](/general-dentistry/digital-x-rays/) of the tooth in question, shown on the screen beside you. Pain is a symptom; the image usually reveals the reason.

items.title: Get you comfortable
items.body: The first goal is to stop the pain and remove the immediate risk: numbing, draining an abscess, smoothing a sharp edge, re-cementing a crown, placing a temporary filling.

items.title: Plan the definitive fix
items.body: Sometimes that is done the same day. Often the lasting repair, a crown or a root canal for example, is scheduled once the tooth has settled. You leave knowing what comes next and what it costs.

sections.heading: What an emergency visit is not
body: It is not an automatic extraction. A tooth that hurts can usually be saved, and we will tell you plainly when it can and when it cannot. It is also not treatment at any hour: booking is online around the clock, but patients are seen during our office hours. The [after-hours page](/emergency-dentistry/after-hours/) explains what to do overnight and when a hospital is the right call.
New patients are welcome for emergencies. You do not need to have been here before, and you can [complete your paperwork online](/new-patients/patient-forms/) on the way in.

faqs.a: Usually, if you call during our hours. We keep room in the schedule for urgent problems, and seven-day hours mean a Saturday morning or a weekday evening is often available. Call rather than booking online for anything that hurts, so we can plan the visit properly.

faqs.q: What should I do for the pain until my appointment?
faqs.a: Rinse gently with warm salt water, floss carefully in case food is trapped, and take an over-the-counter pain reliever exactly as the label directs, if it is safe for you. Do not put aspirin on the gum. A cold compress on the outside of the face helps with swelling. Our [toothache guide](/emergency-dentistry/toothache/) has more.

faqs.q: Do you accept insurance for emergency visits?
faqs.a: Yes, the same plans as for any visit: Aetna, Ameritas, Delta Dental, Humana, Cigna, MetLife and Virginia Medicaid. Bring your card or a photo of it. If you have no insurance, we give you the cost of the exam and any same-day treatment before we start.

cta.heading: Something hurts? Call, and we will plan the visit with you.
cta.body: Describe what happened and whoever answers will tell you how soon you can be seen and what to do in the meantime.
